observation.visible_scene: An industrial workshop interior. A bearded man wearing glasses, a yellow hard hat, a white shirt and a yellow high-visibility vest stands in the foreground holding a tablet in his left hand and a stylus/pen in his right. Two large orange articulated robotic arms with black end-effectors and cabling fill the background, plus a workbench with metal fixtures in the lower left and a window on the right.
visible_changes: At the start (frames 1-5) the man looks down at the tablet, which is held roughly horizontally with its light-colored face angled toward him; the stylus in his right hand points upward.

Between frames 6 and 12 his head lifts and his gaze turns toward the camera while the tablet rotates in his hands from a horizontal position to a vertical one, so that its dark face ends up pointing outward toward the viewer.
From frames 13 to 20 the tablet is drawn in and held upright against his chest/torso, dark side facing the camera; the stylus in his right hand reorients to point downward.

From about frame 20 to the end (frame 41) the man, tablet and stylus remain in a static pose, held against his body, with him looking directly at the camera; only very small postural drift is visible.

Throughout the clip the camera slowly pushes in / zooms: the man and the background robot arms become slightly larger and the framing tightens from frame 1 to frame 41, while the relative layout of the robots to the man stays the same.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the man was doing or reading on the tablet before the segment began, and whether he speaks or moves after the segment ends.
The content or power state of the tablet screen and the exact purpose of the stylus.
Any motion of the robotic arms outside this excerpt (they appear stationary here).
uncertain_details: Whether the dark face shown to the camera is the tablet's screen or its back cover is not fully resolvable; the screen appears black/dark when facing the viewer.
The slight change in the man's position within the frame could be partly his own body movement and partly the camera zoom; the two are hard to separate.
A faint reflection/greenish tint on the tablet in mid-frames may be screen glare rather than a separate object.
